\chapter{Results}
\label{ch:results}

% Written 21 September 2026 from analysis/SPINE.md sections 4, 7b and 8.
% Every number is generated by scripts/dial_results_tables.py and scripts/dial_figures.py from the
% executed records; nothing in this chapter is computed by hand.

This chapter reports the executed dial experiment against the rules fixed in
Chapter~\ref{ch:design}.
Section~\ref{sec:res-executed} states what ran.
Sections~\ref{sec:res-resource} and~\ref{sec:res-acquired} give the two
co-play readouts: what happened to the resource, and what the naive learner
acquired.
Section~\ref{sec:res-decision} applies the pre-registered decision rules,
Section~\ref{sec:res-frozen} the frozen battery, and
Section~\ref{sec:res-m3} the negative control at \(m=3\).
Section~\ref{sec:res-mechanism} asks why the answer came out as it did.

The verdict is stated once, here: on the pre-registered arms the result is a
\textbf{null}.
Neither S nor T holds.
The chapter's substance is not that nothing happened, but what did: at
\(m=2\) every arm whose agent~2 carried chained cross-episode credit drove the
resource to extinction on every seed, while the controls that lack the
objective sustained it; and the exploitative outcome that motivates the
shaping literature appeared only at \(m=3\), where a partner with no trial
objective at all produced it too.

\section{What was executed}
\label{sec:res-executed}

Forty-six training runs of 100 epochs at the live design point
(Chapter~\ref{ch:env}), following \texttt{GATE\_GO} on 16~September
(Section~\ref{sec:gates}): nine arms at \(m=2\) and three at \(m=3\), with
five seeds on the arms that carry the decision and three elsewhere; 38 of
them are the pre-registered arms, the rest the split-credit and history-off
additions.
The five chained-credit arms were run twice, first with the estimator as
executed and then, after the bug of Section~\ref{sec:res-v1} was found,
with the corrected one; unless a section says ``v1'', the chained arms'
numbers are from the corrected run.
% [Until the rerun lands, the chained-arm numbers in this chapter are the v1 values.]
Each trained agent~1 was then frozen and probed for 20 epochs against the
scripted coin-flip partner, and each evaluated shaper entered the frozen
battery E1--E4, whose fresh learners were probed the same way.
One epoch is one trial of five episodes by five parallel games, so a
20-epoch probe scores between 21{,}000 and 25{,}000 live rounds per seed.
Windows are epochs 81--100 throughout.

\section{The resource}
\label{sec:res-resource}

Figure~\ref{fig:outcomes-m2} and Table~\ref{tab:currency} give the co-play
outcome at \(m=2\).
The arms separate into two groups that do not overlap on any seed.

\begin{figure}[ht]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/dial/outcomes_m2.pdf}
\caption{Co-play at \(m=2\) over epochs 81--100.
  Top: the share of episodes whose pool is still alive at round~50.
  Bottom: units received per live round, agent~1 in the light bar and
  agent~2 in the dark bar, against the dotted line at 1.0 that mutual
  restraint pays each player.
  Bars are means over seeds and each marker is one seed.
  Red marks the four arms whose agent~2 carries chained cross-episode
  credit; every one of them collapses the resource, and the three without a
  trial-memory prompt do so on every seed.}
\label{fig:outcomes-m2}
\end{figure}

\textbf{The controls sustain the resource.} Two naive learners kept the pool
alive in 0.96 of episodes and earned 1.15 and 1.18 units per live round,
above the 1.0 that mutual restraint pays and near the 1.25 of the reciprocal
profile (Chapter~\ref{ch:env}).
Both requests were restraint in 0.68 of live rounds.
The trial-batched control reached survival 0.49 with 0.82 and 1.06 units per
round, and the split-credit arm 0.58 with 0.89 and 1.14.

\textbf{The chained-credit arms extinguish it.} Shaper-matched, shaper-slow
and ShapeLLM-style recorded survival \(0.00\) on all thirteen of their seeds.
Both players earned between 0.38 and 0.49 units per round, against the 0.36
that mutual harvest pays: these arms converge on the worst cell in the game.
Mutual restraint fell to between 0.03 and 0.10 of live rounds while mutual
harvest rose to between 0.44 and 0.62.
The fourth chained arm, ShapeLLM-style with the previous-round line removed,
reached survival 0.11.

The gap is not a matter of degree.
No seed of any chained arm reached the survival of the worst control seed.
Table~\ref{tab:currency} averages over seeds; Table~\ref{tab:coplay} gives
every seed separately, including the two control seeds that also collapsed
(trial-batched seed~2 and slow seeds~1 and~2), so the spread within an arm is
visible beside the gap between arms.

\section{What the naive learner acquired}
\label{sec:res-acquired}

The claim is about agent~1's policy, read from the probe
(Section~\ref{sec:method-probe}).
Figure~\ref{fig:classes-m2} counts the classes and
Table~\ref{tab:classes} gives every rate with the number of rounds it rests
on.

\begin{figure}[ht]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/dial/classes_m2.pdf}
\caption{Policy class of the frozen agent~1 at \(m=2\), one bar per arm and
  one unit per seed.
  No arm produced a \emph{conditional} learner, so the teaching outcome T was
  never in play at this design point.
  Classes rest on between 3{,}036 and 7{,}518 rounds in their smallest cell.}
\label{fig:classes-m2}
\end{figure}

Against a naive partner the learner became unconditional on five of five
seeds; against the trial-batched control on four of five; against the
split-credit shaper on four of five.
Against the chained-credit shapers it did not: shaper-matched left it mixed
on four seeds and none on one, shaper-slow mixed on all three, and
ShapeLLM-style mixed on two, none on two and unconditional on one.

Two things follow.
The environment at \(m=2\) teaches unconditional restraint without any
shaping objective, so a difference between a shaper's learner and a control's
was never going to be the evidence that the objective works.
And where the objective changed the learner at all, it changed it away from
restraint.

\input{tables/dial/classes}

\section{The pre-registered decision}
\label{sec:res-decision}

Applying Section~\ref{sec:decide} to those classes
(\texttt{evaluate\_dial.py --decide --length 100}):

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{S fails, and it fails on condition~2.} Condition~1 is satisfied
  for the split-credit arm, whose learner is unconditional on four of five
  seeds, and fails for both pre-registered shapers.
  Condition~2 requires the naive, slow and trial-batched controls not to be
  unconditional; they are, on 5/5, 1/3 and 4/5 seeds.
  Conditions~3 and~4 are treated in Section~\ref{sec:res-frozen}.
\item \textbf{T fails.} It requires a conditional learner against a shaper and
  a none learner against the matching control. No arm at \(m=2\) produced a
  conditional learner at all.
\item \textbf{C passes} (Section~\ref{sec:res-m3}).
\end{itemize}

The verdict on the pre-registered arms is therefore a null, and the
additional split-credit arm is a null on its own line.
No secondary readout rescues either, and none is offered: survival,
return and the joint-request shares are reported above as outcomes, and
Section~\ref{sec:decide} rules them out as evidence for S.

\section{The frozen battery}
\label{sec:res-frozen}

\input{tables/dial/frozen}

Table~\ref{tab:frozen} carries conditions~3 and~4.
A fresh learner trained against the frozen split-credit shaper became
unconditional on five of five seeds; against ShapeLLM-style on one of five;
against shaper-matched on none.
Condition~4 fails everywhere, and for a reason that bears on the whole
design: the replay tape, a recorded stream of the shaper's takes that cannot
respond to the learner, produced unconditional learners on five, four and
five of five seeds.
Whatever teaches restraint here does not need to answer the learner.

E3 exceeded E4 on five of five seeds for split credit, by a wide margin
(1.17 against 0.43 units per round), on four of five for shaper-matched and
three of five for ShapeLLM-style, in both cases by margins under 0.1.

Because E1 exists only for shapers, it cannot yet separate \emph{this
shaper's policy teaches a stranger} from \emph{any trained agent~2 teaches a
stranger}.
The control runs that settle it are specified in the pre-registration's
amendment of 21~September; their classes are reported beside
Table~\ref{tab:frozen} when they land.

\section{The negative control at \texorpdfstring{\(m=3\)}{m = 3}}
\label{sec:res-m3}

\begin{figure}[ht]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/dial/regimes.pdf}
\caption{The same two arms in both regimes, epochs 81--100.
  At \(m=3\) agent~2 out-earns agent~1 and the asymmetric profile dominates
  play, under ShapeLLM-style and under the slow arm alike.
  The slow arm has no trial objective: its agent~2 differs from an ordinary
  naive learner only in learning rate and clip.}
\label{fig:regimes}
\end{figure}

At \(m=3\), where a single player can sustain the pool and commitment wins
(Chapter~\ref{ch:env}), ShapeLLM-style produced the outcome the shaping
literature reports: agent~2 earned 1.81 units per live round against
agent~1's 1.01, with 0.83 of live rounds spent in the asymmetric profile and
survival 0.88.
That is the shape of ShapeLLM's Chicken result on this environment.

The slow arm produced the same signature without any trial objective: 1.73
against 1.21, with the asymmetric profile on 0.59 of rounds.
Decision~C passed --- the slow arm's learner yields on three of three seeds
(\(r_{\mathrm{after\ take}}\) of 0.54, 0.73 and 0.95) --- so by the rule fixed
on 14~September, a yielding or unconditional learner at \(m=3\) is not
evidence for S.

\paragraph{A measurement caveat specific to \(m=3\).}
At that growth rate a restrained pool sits at capacity, so the stock almost
never falls below the probe's cut of 12: between 0.004 and 0.3 per cent of
live rounds for the slow and ShapeLLM-style arms.
Their \(r_{\mathrm{low}}\) therefore rests on 1, 8, 31 or 72 rounds, two
\(m=3\) probes are undetermined, and the class labels there should not be
leaned on.
Decision~C is unaffected: it reads \(r_{\mathrm{after\ take}}\), which rests
on between 10{,}250 and 12{,}340 rounds in every \(m=3\) probe.
The regime is therefore reported on behavioural readouts, with the classes
and their cell sizes confined to Table~\ref{tab:classes}.

\section{The estimator-v1 runs: the measured effect of the bug}
\label{sec:res-v1}

% This section reports the runs made with the estimator as first executed (16--20 September). Their numbers are final.
% The sections above and below are regenerated from the corrected rerun (docs/HANDOVER_RERUN_V2.md); until they are,
% their chained-arm numbers are the v1 values and are labelled as such.

The five chained-credit arms were first run with the estimator described
in Section~\ref{sec:method-estimators} as executed, which bootstraps the
value through the environment's reset at every collapse.
Those runs produced the collapse reported above: survival 0.00 on all
thirteen seeds of the three arms without the previous-round line removed,
both agents earning 0.38 to 0.49 units per round against the 0.36 of
mutual harvest, agent~2's restraint falling monotonically from about 0.25
at the first epoch to 0.07 (shaper-matched) and 0.20 (ShapeLLM-style) at
the hundredth, and a mean collapse round of 12 that never improved while
the controls' rose from 13 to between 40 and 50.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering\small
\caption{The executed chained estimator and the corrected one, replayed on
  each arm's own recorded play over epochs 81--100 with a tabular critic
  fitted to the same data.
  The statistic is the policy-gradient projection toward restraint as a
  \(t\)-value: positive means PPO would push toward restraint.
  ``As run'' bootstraps the value through the reset after a collapse;
  ``value reset'' sets it to zero at each episode's last live step and
  keeps the \(\lambda\)-chain; ``position-aware'' gives the critic the
  round and episode index without the reset.
  Generated by \texttt{scripts/dial\_credit\_replay.py}.}
\label{tab:v1-replay}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
Recorded play, seeds 0 / 1 / 2 & as run & value reset & position-aware critic \\
\midrule
ShapeLLM-style (chained, v1) & \(-19.8\) / \(-20.8\) / \(-18.8\) & \(+20.0\) / \(+21.9\) / \(+20.0\) & \(-19.6\) / \(-20.6\) / \(-18.9\) \\
shaper-matched (chained, v1) & \(-0.5\) / \(-0.8\) / \(-0.9\) & \(+0.6\) / \(+1.1\) / \(+0.7\) & \(-0.5\) / \(-0.7\) / \(-1.0\) \\
shaper-slow (chained, v1) & \(-0.1\) / \(-0.3\) / \(-1.5\) & \(+1.6\) / \(+1.1\) / \(+1.0\) & \(-0.0\) / \(-0.3\) / \(-1.4\) \\
naive arm, agent~1 (episodic; survival 0.96) & \(-2.5\) & \(-2.3\) & --- \\
trial-batched arm, agent~2 (episodic) & \(-1.5\) & \(-0.1\) & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:v1-replay} locates the cause.
On the ShapeLLM-style arm's own play, where agent~2 still restrained on a
fifth of rounds and so left something to credit, the executed estimator's
push is strongly away from restraint on every seed, and setting the
bootstrap to zero at episode ends reverses it to strongly toward restraint
on every seed; on shaper-matched, whose agent~2 had almost stopped
restraining, both signs are near zero.
Giving the critic the round and episode index changes nothing, so this is
not the value head's blindness to position.
On the controls' play, whose episodes end at the horizon rather than by
collapse, the two forms agree.
The inversion is therefore a property of chaining through a collapse into
a fresh pool, and it is self-reinforcing: once collapses are common, the
estimator pushes further from restraint, which makes collapses more
common.
Every chained arm was in that state from its first epoch.

Two consequences are fixed before the corrected results are read.
The v1 collapse is evidence about an estimator, not about the trial-level
objective or about shaping.
And the split-credit arm's difference from shaper-matched, which
Section~\ref{sec:res-mechanism} reports as the estimator carrying the
outcome, has a named mechanism: split credit computes advantages within
episodes and so never bootstraps through a reset.

\section{Why the answer came out this way}
\label{sec:res-mechanism}

\begin{figure}[ht]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/dial/curves_m2.pdf}
\caption{Learning curves at \(m=2\), mean over seeds.
  The chained-credit arms never leave survival 0.00, and their agent~2
  restrains \emph{less} as training proceeds, from about 0.25 at the first
  epoch to 0.07 (shaper-matched) and 0.20 (ShapeLLM-style) at the hundredth.
  The controls and the split-credit arm rise throughout.}
\label{fig:curves-m2}
\end{figure}

Figure~\ref{fig:curves-m2} rules out the first explanation a reader will
reach for.
The chained arms did not run out of budget: their agent~2 moved away from
restraint monotonically, and the survival curve is flat at zero from the
first epoch to the last.
A longer run extrapolates away from the claim, not toward it.

Three measurements locate the failure in the estimator rather than the game.

\textbf{The environment is learnable.} Gate G1 showed a naive learner
acquiring restraint against a committed harvester at \(m=3\) (0.967, 0.989,
0.958) and G2 reciprocity against tit-for-tat at \(m=2\) (0.907, 0.982,
0.916), both before any arm was run (Section~\ref{sec:gates}).
The controls above acquire restraint in co-play.

\textbf{The trial objective has no channel specific to it.}
Table~\ref{tab:channel} reports, for every trial and pair of consecutive
episodes, the correlation between agent~2's restraint in an episode and
agent~1's change in restraint into the next.
Most seeds read none, and where a positive partial correlation appears it
appears in the naive and trial-batched arms too (0.13 to 0.26).
The within-trial response is a property of the environment's dynamics, not
of the objective.

\input{tables/dial/channel}

\textbf{The estimator carries the difference.} Split credit and
shaper-matched differ in nothing but how cross-episode credit is estimated
(Chapter~\ref{ch:method}): the same seat, speed, schedule, batch and prompt.
Split credit sustains the resource and leaves an unconditional learner;
chained credit extinguishes it.
The pilot diagnosis before training found the same asymmetry in the
estimates themselves --- whole-trial advantages with a standard deviation of
14 to 32 against a naive learner's 2 to 7, and a restrain-minus-harvest gap
never significant over ten blocks (Section~\ref{sec:gates}).

\section{What this chapter licenses}
\label{sec:res-licenses}

In an environment built so that a shaper has something to buy, and
verified before training to be learnable by this stack, the trial-level
shaping objective as ShapeLLM instantiates it did not change what a
co-learning agent acquired, except by making it worse; with chained
whole-trial credit it destroyed the resource the claim is about on every
seed; and the exploitative outcome that motivates the literature appeared
only in the regime where a partner with no trial objective produces it too.

What the chapter does not license is equally definite.
It does not show that opponent shaping fails for language-model agents in
general: one base model, one adapter rank, one environment family, 100
epochs, three to five seeds.
It does not show that the objective is unlearnable, only that this estimator
of it did not learn.
And it does not license reading the split-credit arm as a positive result:
that arm matched its controls, it did not beat them.
